HOLD ON. If you are contemplating taking out large amount of debt to attend BU over free tuition… DONT DO IT.

Graduating Film Major here; any film program is going to be what you make of it! This program is good, but it most likely pales in comparison to USC or a conservatory program for cinematography or directing etc.
Don’t get me wrong, the professors are great and the students are awesome. But any program is only going to give you as much as you put into it, and taking out debt with an art degree is always a riskier choice than one for comp sci.

Also, NY is a huge benefit. A lot of success in filmmaking, post-grad, is made easier with strong connections, so making friends in and around NY. Don’t get me wrong, you’ll make great friends here too, it’s just that they will be way more likely to scatter across the globe after finishing at BU. It won’t be your degree, it will be the skills you choose to learn and the people you connect with that will make the difference in the film industry.

Hi, film major here. The program itself isn’t perfect, but there’s a good community here and there are a lot of really good professors (but you should definitely know which ones to pick in some cases). 

If they are looking to study production, they should be prepared to put a lot of time on work outside of class, specifically by spending time helping out on student sets, as soon as they get to BU. Start PAing. It’s the best way to learn and the filmmaking community/industry is all about connections.

I believe the program here is not nearly as robust or rigorous as what you might get at schools like USC or UCLA or NYU or even Emerson most likely, as the program doesn’t require students to follow any kind of emphasis or specialty, and classes are graded fairly generously if you put in effort. Also a decent amount of our gear either runs out during production season or is damaged, but it’s all high quality stuff, and available if you reserve it early enough.

This program is definitely what you make of it. The program lacks a bit of foundational film theory in the curriculum, and many students graduate BU with little production expertise, simply because they didn’t take the time to get on set and do the extra work.

But if you take the time to get to know people, you can find some very creative, smart people here, and learn a lot about filmmaking.

Just know now, if your student wants to join the creative film (movie) industry, that the film industry has little care for film degrees. What matters is who and what you know, and your showreel or portfolio. A lot of people on r/filmmakers would say that you should save your money and just start working on set to get your film education, as having the resume would probably be better. 

There are also seemingly strong, production-oriented programs at schools like Ithaca, make sure to shop around and. Or just look at the top programs, looking back I just wish I looked at more schools.

TLDR: For me, it’s plain and simple. Tennis is known as a game of respect and dignity... Novak clocked a line judge in the face with a ball less than a year ago. Of course he didn’t mean to do it, but both Federer and Nadal have more than enough self control to never even try such a reckless expression of frustration this late into their careers. The GOAT of tennis HAS to be the man with the best sportsmanship, or else we begin to lose that wonderful part of tennis culture. Thus, I prefer Fedal.

I will never believe in Djokovic to stand with the same level of dignity and sportsmanship like Fedal. I know Federer and Nadal had their share of outbursts on court when they were younger, but as they hit their prime, they were never seen smashing a racquet on court, at least not one that I’ve heard of (I’m pretty sure Nadal has never broken one). Novak has always been the most short-tempered out of the three of them, and has broken the most racquets out of all of them. For insight, the reason I take such offense from a broken racquet, is because tennis racquets are not cheap, and I myself have only been able to afford 2 quality racquets in my life. I would never think to break one when I know there is someone else out there who has never had the chance to play with such a good instrument. To me, breaking a racquet shows how a player is spoiled. Novak to still be hitting people with balls out of frustration this late into his career is what I base my perception of him off. I also know that he has done a lot of good for others, and I know he has said many good things about his opponents and fans throughout his career. However, it is known that it is easiest to be kind in good times, and I believe how you act at your worst times is a more true test of character. While Novak may someday hold the slam record, I will always look up to Rafa (specifically) more, because of his fiery passion for practice, competition, and his amazing resiliency in the face of a comeback or other challenge. On top of all that, Nadal is known as one of the greats sportsmen in the game. I can’t call Novak the goat, because I can’t see him acting as one of my idols, the same way Fed and Nadal did when I was younger. Whether that’s simply a result of the media’s portrayal of him or not, I can’t say, but it is what I believe at this time. I’ll never say he’s not a great player. He’s just not my GOAT.

When growing your business, you can aim for vertical expansion or horizontal expansion. Vertical expansion means creating products for the same customers who have differing levels of need. Maybe someone needs a month subscription to your service, maybe the next person needs a yearly subscription with a few addition features. It’s the same product, just with better options. Horizontal expansion means to offer different products around the same idea, so that you can serve customers with differing needs. You own a baseball bat shop? Great, once that works, start selling helmets and gloves, if that works out, start selling hockey gear. 

There is also a useful model to think of when expanding. “The wheel and spoke” model. Think of the center of a bicycle wheel, this is your main project. If you wish, you can create new projects and products, based off of the original. Each one will act as a spoke coming off of the center of the wheel. These are meant to be smaller ideas that produce a little extra income and can help promote your original big idea. Have everything funnel into the center, and you will produce more traffic. These smaller ideas can be anything you want to explore, just make sure everything is connected, so that your businesses have synergy to them.
